Rashi on Nedarim 36b:1:1.hebrew: כיון דזכות הוא לו - שמרויח שתורם עליו משלו, ולא צריך ליתן לו כלום:
Rashi on Nedarim 36b:1:1.english: Since it is a benefit for him - For he profits in that [the other person] separates terumah on his behalf from his own [produce], and [the owner] does not need to give him anything.

Rashi on Nedarim 36b:1:2.english: It does not require knowledge - For one may benefit a person in his absence.

Rashi on Nedarim 36b:1:3.hebrew: או דלמא - כיון דמצוה דיליה היא — דבעל הכרי — ניחא ליה למיעבדיה, שיקיים הוא את המצוה; לפיכן צריך שיודיעו:
Rashi on Nedarim 36b:1:3.english: Or perhaps - Since it is his mitzvah — [that] of the owner of the pile [of produce] — it is preferable for him to perform it, so that he [himself] fulfills the mitzvah; therefore, he must inform him.

Rashi on Nedarim 36b:2:1.english: If we say - [that he separates terumah] from [the produce] of the owner of the pile for [that of] the owner of the pile.

Rashi on Nedarim 36b:2:2.hebrew: אילימא לדעתיה דיליה - לדעתו של תורם, שלא הודיעו לבעל הכרי שהוא תורם עליו:
Rashi on Nedarim 36b:2:2.english: If we say with his [own] knowledge - With the knowledge of the one separating teruma, [meaning] that he did not inform the owner of the pile that he is separating teruma for him.

Rashi on Nedarim 36b:2:3.hebrew: מאן שוייה שליח - הא קיימא לן, מה אתם לדעתכם, אף שלוחכם לדעתכם:
Rashi on Nedarim 36b:2:3.english: Who made him an agent - For it is established for us: "Just as you [act] with your [own] knowledge, so too your agent [acts] with your knowledge."

Rashi on Nedarim 36b:3:1.english: Isn't he benefiting him, as he is performing his agency - And he [the one tithing] had forbidden him [benefit by a vow].

Rashi on Nedarim 36b:3:2.english: Isn't he benefiting him - this [person] who separates terumah on his behalf.

Rashi on Nedarim 36b:3:3.english: Rather, is it not on his own knowledge - That he did not inform the owner of the pile that he wants to separate terumah on his behalf.

Rashi on Nedarim 36b:3:4.hebrew: וא"א צריך דעת, הא קמהני ליה - כיון שתורם עליו בידיעתו, הא קמהני ליה:
Rashi on Nedarim 36b:3:4.english: And if you say [it] requires knowledge, isn’t he benefiting him - Since he separates [terumah] on his behalf with his knowledge, isn’t he benefiting him?

Rashi on Nedarim 36b:3:5.hebrew: אלא לאו אין צריך דעת - ולהכי תורם עליו, דכיון שתורם עליו שלא מדעתו, לא מהני ליה כלל:
Rashi on Nedarim 36b:3:5.english: Rather, [is it] not [that it] does not require [the owner's] knowledge - And therefore he separates teruma on his behalf, for since he separates teruma on his behalf without his knowledge, he does not benefit him at all.

Rashi on Nedarim 36b:4:1.hebrew: לעולם משל בעל הכרי - מיירי, ולדעתו דבעל הכרי. ודקאמרת: הא קמהני ליה דעביד שליחותיה ותרים:
Rashi on Nedarim 36b:4:1.english: Actually, [it is] from [the produce] of the owner of the pile - [It] is speaking [of this case], and with the consent of the owner of the pile. And [as for] what you might say, "Behold, he is benefiting him in that he performs his agency and separates teruma."

Rashi on Nedarim 36b:4:2.hebrew: באומר כל הרוצ' לתרום יבא ויתרום - דכיון דלא שויה שליח ממש טפי מאחריני, ואחריני נמי יכולין לתרום כמותו, לא מהני ליה כלל, דאי לא תרים ליה האי, תרים ליה איניש אחרינא. ומהכא ליכא למשמע מינה כלל:
Rashi on Nedarim 36b:4:2.english: Where one says: Anyone who wishes to separate terumah may come and separate terumah - For since he did not make him an actual agent more than others, and others can also separate terumah just like him, he does not benefit him at all, for if this one does not separate terumah for him, another person will separate terumah for him. And from here, nothing can be inferred from it at all.

Rashi on Nedarim 36b:5:1.hebrew: טובת הנאה משל מי - אותה פרוטה שיכול לקבל מישראל אחר כדי ליתנה לבן בתו כהן, משל מי היא:
Rashi on Nedarim 36b:5:1.english: Whose is the discretionary benefit - That perutah that one can receive from another Israelite in order to give it [the terumah] to his daughter's son [who is] a priest, whose is it?

Rashi on Nedarim 36b:5:2.hebrew: אי לאו פירי דהאי - דתורם, לא מתקן כריא דההוא, ותיהוי אותה פרוטה דתורם:
Rashi on Nedarim 36b:5:2.english: If not for the produce of this one - [i.e.,] of the one who separates [teruma], the pile of that [other] one would not be made fit, and [therefore] that perutah [belongs] to the one who separates [teruma].

Rashi on Nedarim 36b:5:3.english: Or perhaps not, etc. - And the discretionary benefit belongs to the owner of the pile.

Rashi on Nedarim 36b:6:1.hebrew: את כל תבואת זרעך ונתת ונו' - שמע מינה דבעל הכרי היא טובת הנאה, מדכתיב זרעך ונתת:
Rashi on Nedarim 36b:6:1.english: All the produce of your seed, and you shall give, etc. - We learn from this that the benefit of discretion [in giving it] belongs to the owner of the pile, since it is written: "your seed" [and] "and you shall give."

Rashi on Nedarim 36b:7:1.hebrew: תורם את תרומותיו ומעשרותיו לדעתו - של תורם. וקס"ד דמשלו על של בעל הכרי, הא קא מהני ליה, דשקיל טובת הנאה:
Rashi on Nedarim 36b:7:1.english: He separates his teruma and his tithes with his knowledge - [meaning, with the knowledge] of the one separating [it]. And it was initially assumed that [he separates] from his own [produce] on behalf of [that] of the owner of the pile; [thus,] isn't he benefiting him, since he receives [the] discretionary benefit?

Rashi on Nedarim 36b:7:2.hebrew: אלא - מדתורם לו, שמע מינה דטובת הנאה של תורם היא:
Rashi on Nedarim 36b:7:2.english: Rather - Since he separates teruma for him, conclude from it that the discretionary benefit belongs to the one who separates teruma.

Rashi on Nedarim 36b:7:3.hebrew: אמרי - לעולם מהא ליכא למשמע מיניה טובת הנאה של מי, דהכא לא מיירי אלא בשל בעל הכרי ולדעתו דבעל הכרי, ולהכי טובת הנאה שלו, ואפילו הכי לא קא מהני ליה:
Rashi on Nedarim 36b:7:3.english: They say - Actually, from this [mishna] one cannot infer to whom the discretionary benefit belongs, for here it is speaking only of [the produce] of the owner of the pile, and with the knowledge of the owner of the pile, and therefore the discretionary benefit is his; and even so, he is not benefiting him.

Rashi on Nedarim 36b:7:4.english: Where he says, "Anyone who wishes, etc." - As we established above.

Rashi on Nedarim 36b:8:1.hebrew: המקדיש - שפודה את הקדשו, מוסיף חומש ולא אדם אחר, כדכתיב: "ואם המקדיש יגאל את ביתו" (ויקרא כז):
Rashi on Nedarim 36b:8:1.english: The one who consecrates - [the one] who redeems his consecrated [property] adds one-fifth, and not another person, as it is written: "And if the one who consecrates redeems his house" (Leviticus 27).

Rashi on Nedarim 36b:8:2.hebrew: ומתכפר עושה תמורה - המפריש קרבן לפטור חובתו של חבירו, המתכפר עושה תמורה באותו קרבן, דהשתא הוי דידיה, ולא המפרישו, דמאחר שהפריש לצורכו, קנאו המתכפר:
Rashi on Nedarim 36b:8:2.english: And the one seeking atonement renders a substitute - [When] one sets aside an offering to discharge his fellow's obligation, the one seeking atonement renders a substitute with that offering, for now it is his, and not the one who set it aside, since once he set [it] aside for his [fellow's] need, the one seeking atonement has acquired it.

Rashi on Nedarim 36b:8:3.english: And one who separates [teruma], etc., the discretionary benefit is his - [It belongs] to the one who separates [the teruma].

Rashi on Nedarim 36b:9:1.hebrew: שנוטלין שכר על לימוד המקרא וכו' - ולהכי לא ילמדנו מקרא בחנם לזה, דקמהני ליה השכר שהיה לו ליתן, אבל מלמדו הלכות בחנם, דלא קא מהני ליה כלל:
Rashi on Nedarim 36b:9:1.english: [In a place] where one takes payment for teaching Bible, etc. - And therefore he may not teach Bible for free to this [person], since he benefits him [with] the payment that he would have had to give; but he teaches him halakhot for free, since he does not benefit him at all.

Rashi on Nedarim 36b:9:2.hebrew: מאי פסקא - דבמנהגא תליא מילתא, ולאו איסורא איכא אפי' למשקל שכר של המקרא? תריץ: לא, ודאי לאו שפיר עבד דשקל כלל:
Rashi on Nedarim 36b:9:2.english: Why [was it stated] categorically - [Does this mean] that the matter depends on custom, and there is no prohibition even to take payment for [teaching] Bible? [The Gemara] answers: No, certainly one who takes [payment] at all does not act properly.

Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:1:1.hebrew: ותורם תרומתו לדעתו - בגמ' מפרש לדעת מאן:
Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:1:1.english: And he separates his terumah with his knowledge - In the Gemara, it explains whose knowledge [is meant].

Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:1:2.hebrew: מי אמרינן כיון דזכות הוא לא צריך דעת - דזכין לאדם שלא בפניו, וזכיה מטעם שליחות — שפיר הוי שליחותא. והא דאמרינן בכל דוכתא דזכייה מטעם שליחות, מהכא תניא ליה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:1:2.english: Do we say, "Since it is a benefit, it does not require knowledge"? - For one may act in a person's interest in his absence, and [since] zechiyah [acting on another's behalf operates] on the principle of agency, it is a valid agency. And that which we say everywhere, that zechiyah [operates] on the principle of agency, is taught from here.

Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:2:1.english: If we say - from [the produce] of the owner of the pile for [that of] the owner of the pile.

Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:2:2.english: Who designated him an agent - And why does he separate teruma?

Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:3:1.hebrew: אלא לדעתו דבעל הכרי הא קא מהני ליה דעביד שליחותיה - כיון דהוא ידע הוי כמו שמצוהו, ואיכא איסורא. ודאי אי לאו בדעתו לא הוה איסורא, דמשום המצוה שרי; אבל לדעתו דבעל [הכרי], מכי ידע ביה הוי כמו שמצוהו והוי שלוחו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:3:1.english: Rather, [it is] with the knowledge of the owner of the pile — isn't he benefiting him by performing his agency? - Since he [the owner] knows, it is as though he commands him, and there is a prohibition. Certainly, if it were not with his knowledge, there would be no prohibition, for on account of the mitzvah it is permitted; but with the knowledge of the owner of [the pile], once he knows about it, it is as though he commands him and he is his agent.

Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:3:2.english: Isn't he benefiting him - [Through] this [act] that he separates terumah on his behalf.

Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:3:3.hebrew: אלא לאו אין צריך דעת - והא דאמרינן (בב"מ כב -): "מה אתם לדעתכם, אף שלוחכם לדעתכם", י"ל דהיינו כשתורם משל בעל הכרי, אבל בתורם משלו אז אין צריך דעת. וא"ת: מיהו קשה לרב, דההיא דשוקל שקלו אמאי צריך לאוקמא בהפריש ואבד? אפי' בלא הפריש ואבד נמי, דמצוה קעביד כי הכא! צ"ע. מיהו ק"ק: מאי שנא גבי תורם, דמצריך דעת לתרום, אסור דשליחותיה קא עביד, וגבי מחזיר אבידתו או ללמדו תורה, אפילו לדעת יהא אסור כיון שאין מצוה לו? ושמא יש לומר: דבתורם בתרומה, דהדבר תלוי בשליחות, דאין יכול לתרום בלא דעתו, ושייך ביה "שליחותיה קעביד" טפי מאבידה דמתני', וגם מצוה איכא פורתא למבין:
Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:3:3.english: Rather, is it not [that] one does not require knowledge [and consent] - And [as for] that which we say (in Bava Metzia 22a): "Just as you [act] with your knowledge, so too your agent [must act] with your knowledge," one can say that that is when he separates teruma from [the produce] of the owner of the pile, but when he separates from his own [produce], then [it] does not require knowledge [and consent]. And if you ask: However, it is difficult for Rav — regarding that [case] of "he pays his shekel," why does [he] need to establish it as referring to where he separated [it] and it was lost? Even without having separated and lost [it] as well, [it should be permitted,] since he is performing a mitzvah, like here! [This] requires further study. However, it is somewhat difficult: What is the difference regarding one who separates teruma, that [if] he requires knowledge [and consent] to separate teruma, it is forbidden because "he is performing his agency," whereas regarding one who returns his lost object or teaches him Torah, even with [his] knowledge [and consent] it should be forbidden, since he does not instruct him? Perhaps one can say: that with one who separates teruma, since the matter depends on agency — for he cannot separate teruma without his knowledge — "he is performing his agency" applies to it more than to [returning] a lost object of the Mishnah; and there is also a bit of a mitzvah, for one who understands.

Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:4:1.hebrew: משל בעל הכרי - תימה, דהכא משמע כיון דאמר "כל הרוצה לתרום" לא מהני ליה; ובפרק המדיר בכתובות (דף ע:), גבי "המדיר אשתו מליהנות לה עד ל' יום יעמיד פרנס", ופריך: "ופרנס לאו שליחותיה קעביד?" ומשני: "באומר 'כל הזן אינו מפסיד'". ופריך: "וכי אמר הכי לאו שליחותיה קעביד? והתנן: מי שהיה מושלך בבור ואמר 'כל השומע קולו יכתוב גט לאשתו'!". ומשני: "מי קאמר 'יזון'? 'כל הזן' קאמר!". אלמא דאי אמר "כ"ל השומע יזון", שייך למימר שליחותיה קעביד! ויש לומר: "כל השומע" משמע לשון שליחות ציווי, אבל "כל הרוצה" אינו לשון ציווי, כ"א מי שיחפוץ יתרום. ור"י אמר: דודאי התם הוא דמיתסר אם אמר "יזון", דשליחותיה קעביד דקא מהני ליה שזן אשתו ומוותר לה פרנסה, דמצוה לפרנס אשתו; אבל בשמעתא דתורם משל בעל הכרי ולא משלו, ובדין הוא דאיסורא ליכא — דאי משום דתורם ליה, מצוה קעביד, כדמתני "ומחזיר לו אבידתו", אלא משום דכיון דבתרומה צריך דעת, הוי כמו שלוחו דמצווהו "לך ותרום"; וכיון דרבנן הפקיעו תורת השליחות מיניה, שפיר עביד. וראיה לדבר, דאמרינן "לעולם משל בעל הכרי" וכדרבא, ול"ק "לעולם משלו" וכדרבא; אלא ש"מ דמשלו, אפי' אומר "כל הרוצה", איסורא איכא, כי ההיא דהמדיר, שהמפרנס מפרנס אשתו משלו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:4:1.english: "From [the produce] of the owner of the pile" - This is astonishing, for here it implies that since he said, "Anyone who wishes to separate terumah," it does not benefit him [i.e., it is not considered a forbidden benefit]. Yet in chapter HaMadir in Ketubot (70b), regarding [the Mishnah]: "One who vows that his wife may not derive benefit from him, for up to thirty days he may appoint a provider," [the Gemara] asks: "And does the provider not act as his agent?" And it answers: "[It refers to a case] where he says, 'Anyone who sustains [her] will not lose out.'" And [the Gemara] asks: "And when he says this, does he not act as his agent? Have we not learned [in a Mishnah]: One who was cast into a pit and said, 'Anyone who hears his voice shall write a bill of divorce for his wife' [may do so]?!" And it answers: "Did he say, 'Let him sustain'? He said, 'Anyone who sustains'!" Thus [we see] that if he said, "Anyone who hears may sustain [her]," it is relevant to say that he acts as his agent! And one can answer: "Anyone who hears" implies an expression of agency and command, whereas "Anyone who wishes" is not an expression of command, rather whoever desires may separate terumah. And Rabbeinu Yitzchak said: Certainly there [in Ketubot] it is forbidden if he said "Let him sustain," because he acts as his agent and thereby benefits him by sustaining his wife and providing her sustenance, for it is a mitzvah [an obligation] to sustain one's wife. However, in our passage, where he separates terumah from [the produce] of the owner of the pile and not from his own, by right there is no prohibition [on account of benefit]—for if [you object] because he separates terumah for him, he is performing a mitzvah, just as [the Mishnah] teaches: "And he may return his lost object to him"—rather, [any prohibition would only be] because, since terumah requires [the owner's] knowledge and consent, he is like his agent whom he commands, "Go and separate terumah"; and once the Rabbis removed the status of agency from him [when he speaks this way], he acts properly. And a proof for this matter is that we say [in the Gemara], "Actually, from [the produce] of the owner of the pile," and like Rava['s statement], and it does not say, "Actually, from his own," and like Rava['s statement]. Rather, learn from this that [if he separates] from his own [produce], even if [the owner] says, "Anyone who wishes [may separate]," there is a prohibition, just like that [case] in [chapter] HaMadir, where the provider sustains his wife from his own [funds].

Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:4:2.hebrew: כל הרוצה - אפילו אחר מצי תרים ליה; הלכך דעת איכא, שליחותא ליכא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:4:2.english: "Anyone who wishes" - Even another person can separate terumah for him; therefore, there is consent, [but] there is no agency.

Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:5:1.english: Whose is the discretionary benefit - That another Israelite gives him a dinar so that he will give [the teruma] to his daughter's son, [who is] a priest.

Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:5:2.english: Or perhaps not, etc. - And the discretionary benefit belongs to the owner of the pile.

Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:7:1.hebrew: איתיביה תורם תרומותיו לדעתו - קס"ד השתא, כדפירש לעיל: משלו על של בעל הכרי קאמר, וא"צ דעת; ואי אמרת טובת הנאה של בעל הכרי — מהני ליה בתרומה זו שוה דינר שיתן לו ישראל. הכא במאי עסקינן? דאמר "כל הרוצה לתרום יבא ויתרום", ומיירי דתורם משל בעל הכרי על של בעל הכרי:
Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:7:1.english: He raised an objection to him: "He separates his terumot with his knowledge" - Currently we assume, as [the Gemara] explained above, [that] it is speaking of [separating] from his own [produce] on behalf of the owner of the pile, and he does not need [the owner's] consent; and if you say [that] the discretionary benefit belongs to the owner of the pile — he benefits him with this terumah, [which is] worth a dinar that an Israelite would give him. With what case are we dealing here? Where he says, "Anyone who wishes to separate terumah may come and separate terumah," and it is speaking of [a case] where he separates from the owner of the pile's [produce] on behalf of the owner of the pile's [produce].

Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:7:2.hebrew: תורם את תרומותיו ומעשרותיו לדעתו - של תורם. וקס"ד דמשלו על של בעל הכרי — הא קא מהני ליה, דשקיל טובת הנאה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:7:2.english: "He separates his teruma and his tithes with his knowledge" - [i.e., the knowledge] of the one separating teruma. And we initially assumed that [he separates] from his own [produce] for [the produce] of the owner of the pile — [if so,] isn't he benefiting him, since he [the owner of the pile] receives the discretionary benefit?

Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:7:3.hebrew: אלא - מדתורם לו, שמע מינה דטובת הנאה של תורם היא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:7:3.english: Rather - Since he separates terumah for him, conclude from this that the discretionary benefit belongs to the one separating terumah.

Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:7:4.hebrew: אמרי - לעולם מהא ליכא למשמע מיניה טובת הנאה של מי, דהכא לא מיירי אלא בשל בעל הכרי ולדעתו דבעל הכרי, ולהכי טובת הנאה שלו, ואפילו הכי לא קא מהני ליה. באומר כל הרוצה בו' — כדאוקימנא לעיל:
Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:7:4.english: [The Sages] say - Actually, from this [mishna] one cannot infer whose the discretionary benefit is, for here it is speaking only of [separating] from [the produce] of the owner of the pile and with the knowledge of the owner of the pile, and therefore the discretionary benefit is his, and even so he is not benefiting him. [It is] where he says, "Anyone who wishes [to separate teruma], etc." — as we established above.

Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:8:1.hebrew: המקדיש - בהמה על מנת שיתכפר בו חבירו, המקדיש מוסיף חומש, דחומש תלאו הכתוב במקדיש, דכתיב: "ואם המקדיש יגאל את ביתו". ומתכפר עושה תמורה — ובפ"ק דתמורה (דף י.) מפרש טעמא מקרא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:8:1.english: The one who consecrates - [i.e., one who consecrates] an animal on condition that his fellow receives atonement through it, the one who consecrates adds one-fifth, for Scripture made the [obligation of] one-fifth dependent upon the one who consecrates, as it is written: "And if the one who consecrates will redeem his house." And the one seeking atonement renders [another animal] a substitute — and in the first chapter of Temurah (10a), [the Gemara] explains the reason from a verse.

Tosafot on Nedarim 36b:8:2.english: And one who separates terumah from his own [produce] for that of his fellow, the discretionary benefit is his:
